paper_metadata.title: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Simulation Architecture for Catastrophe Tail Risk and Portfolio Optimization

summary: The paper proposes a hybrid architecture using Quantum Amplitude Estimation on an 8‑qubit state‑vector simulator to estimate catastrophe tail risk for a synthetic hurricane portfolio. The authors report equivalent tail precision using 7.5×10^5 quantum shots versus 2.0×10^8 classical Monte Carlo samples (96.25% reduction in sample complexity) and a 35% reduction in estimator variance at the 99.5th percentile, yielding VaR estimates of $32.0M ± $0.8M compared to a classical baseline of $37.3M ± $4.1M.

experiments.description: Hybrid catastrophe tail-risk simulation using Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) with zero-noise extrapolation on an 8-qubit state-vector simulator, benchmarked against classical Monte Carlo for a synthetic Florida coastal hurricane portfolio.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) with zero-noise extrapolation and symmetry verification

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Loss distribution parameters were mapped to an 8-qubit register; tail-weighted amplitude encoding concentrated resolution around extreme percentiles.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate tail-risk metrics (VaR and TVaR) for catastrophe loss distributions with reduced estimator variance relative to classical Monte Carlo.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Classical constraint simulation with copula-based correlation models and time-series constraints applied after quantum sampling; ZNE and symmetry verification used for mitigation.

problem_instance.description: Synthetic Florida coastal hurricane portfolio for catastrophe tail-risk estimation and reinsurance portfolio optimization.

dataset_specification.description: Based on HURDAT2, Holland B wind-field parameterization, NWS-23 forward-speed asymmetry, HAZUS vulnerability data; exact portfolio size not reported.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Physics-informed calibration of hurricane tracks, wind speeds, downscaling to over-land gusts, mapping to vulnerability functions, then tail-weighted amplitude encoding.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Benchmark against classical Monte Carlo baseline; reported VaR/TVaR and estimator variance at the 99.5th percentile.

implementation_details.transpilation_target: state-vector simulator with noise profiles representative of superconducting QPUs
implementation_details.classical_solver: classical Monte Carlo baseline; classical copula/VAR/ARIMA constraint simulation; convex optimization and local search for portfolio optimization
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Physics-based catastrophe calibration, deterministic transformations, copula correlation modeling, VAR/ARIMA temporal correlation modeling, min-max normalization in scheduler and objective function.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Tail Metrics Engine computes VaR/TVaR and confidence bands; Portfolio Optimizer computes capital efficiency and treaty structure.

speedup_claims.conditions: synthetic Florida coastal hurricane portfolio; 8-qubit register; 7.5 × 10^5 quantum shots vs 2.0 × 10^8 classical samples
speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as sample efficiency, not wall-clock runtime; includes ZNE overhead and shallow-circuit NISQ constraints.
Paper notes practical implementation has ~53× constant-factor overhead relative to idealized QAE query count.

complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: ~53× overhead relative to idealized QAE query count, due to NISQ constraints and ZNE repetitions
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: 7.5 × 10^5 quantum shots; paper also states idealized QAE would require ≈1,414 queries for the benchmark

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; paper compares 7.5×10^5 quantum shots to 2.0×10^8 classical Monte Carlo samples but does not analyze runtime crossover.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Fault‑tolerant implementation of QAE with far fewer repetitions (≈1,414 ideal queries claimed by authors) and large‑scale logical qubit registers capable of preparing realistic catastrophe loss distributions; significantly deeper circuits than an 8‑qubit toy encoding.
limiting_factors: Experiment performed only on an 8‑qubit state‑vector simulator with synthetic data
Reported advantage concerns sample complexity rather than wall‑clock runtime
Comparison baseline is naive Monte Carlo rather than advanced variance‑reduction methods commonly used in practice
Large constant‑factor overhead (~53× vs ideal QAE queries) due to NISQ noise mitigation
State preparation for realistic loss distributions not analyzed

notes: The paper explicitly states an 8-qubit register and that the hybrid pipeline was executed on a state-vector simulator with noise profiles representative of superconducting QPUs.
The paper reports 7.5 × 10^5 quantum shots and 2.0 × 10^8 classical Monte Carlo samples; the latter is a classical baseline, not a separate experiment.
No explicit circuit depth, gate counts, optimizer, or framework are reported.
Authors highlight a 96.25% reduction in sample complexity and 35% variance reduction but explicitly state this reflects algorithmic query counts rather than runtime.
Results are obtained on a noisy state‑vector simulator rather than actual quantum hardware.
No demonstration that the quantum approach outperforms optimized classical risk‑simulation methods in practice.

experiments.description: Hybrid portfolio optimization using tail-risk metrics from the QAE pipeline to select a non-proportional reinsurance structure via classical optimization.

algorithm.variant: Classical portfolio optimization driven by quantum-derived tail metrics
algorithm.optimizer: continuous convex optimization followed by discrete local search refinement
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial reinsurance layer structure initialized via continuous convex optimization

problem_formulation.objective_function: CE = W1(CoverageRatio) - W2(CapitalLoad) - W3(CededPremium) - W4(LossVolatility), with all terms min-max normalized to [0,1] relative to TIV.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Predefined treaty constraints and minimum regulatory solvency ratios; discrete local search refinement after convex initialization.

problem_instance.description: Reinsurance treaty optimization for the same synthetic Florida coastal hurricane portfolio.

dataset_specification.description: Optimal non-proportional structure with $10.0M attachment point, $50.0M limit, and two reinstatements at 100% premium.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Uses refined hybrid tail metrics (VaR/TVaR) from the QAE experiment as inputs to the optimizer.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Reported Capital Efficiency score compared against a baseline manual structuring of 0.35; optimized score 0.42.

implementation_details.classical_solver: continuous convex optimization and discrete local search
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Tail-risk metrics from the QAE pipeline are used as inputs.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Capital Efficiency score computed and compared to baseline manual structuring.

speedup_claims.caveats: This stage is classical optimization driven by quantum-derived tail metrics; no separate gate-based quantum speedup is reported.

limiting_factors: Experiment is purely classical optimization and contains no gate-based quantum computation

notes: This is a classical optimization stage driven by quantum-derived metrics; no separate gate-based quantum circuit, qubit count, or hardware is reported.
The paper reports the CE objective and the optimized treaty parameters, but the optimization itself is classical.
The portfolio optimization stage is classical and therefore outside the gate-based quantum experiment scope.
